This is a worked example for review of the form of the wording specgen writes.
The subject is the monadic operations of =optional<T&>=, [[https://eel.is/c++draft/optional.ref.monadic][[optional.ref.monadic]​]], whose description mixes /Constraints/, /Mandates/ and /Effects: Equivalent to/ that can be read out of an implementation with prose that cannot.
The code is Beman optional's, cut down to the three members.

Everything shown below is transcluded from this directory: the header, the script that ran specgen, and the files the script wrote.
Nothing is retyped, so what the page shows is what the tool produced.

* Rendered output
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: rendered-output
:END:

Each backend's output is source for a different paper framework.
These are the same files as below, typeset by the framework they are written for.

| Backend | Typeset by | The wording | Marked against the draft |
|---------+------------+-------------+--------------------------|
| =latex= | wg21-latex, the working draft's macros | [[file:rendered/wording.pdf][wording.pdf]] | [[file:rendered/diff.pdf][diff.pdf]] |
| =mpark= | mpark/wg21 | [[file:rendered/wording.mpark.html][wording.mpark.html]] | [[file:rendered/diff.mpark.html][diff.mpark.html]] |
| =org= | wg21org | [[file:rendered/wording.org.html][wording.org.html]] | [[file:rendered/diff.org.html][diff.org.html]] |

=render.sh= builds them into =rendered/=, which is committed so the pages can be opened on GitHub, and records each framework's revision there in =frameworks.txt=.
Each framework is a checkout named by an environment variable, and one that is not named is skipped; the script is [[#typesetting-the-wording][below]].

Two of the six need one change to what specgen wrote before their framework will typeset them at all.
=render.sh= makes each change and says so when it does:

- =diff.pdf=: a changed run of code is not escaped for LaTeX, and the =&= in =using U = invoke_result_t<F, T&>;= stops the build, so =render.sh= escapes it ([[https://github.com/steve-downey/specgen/issues/410][#410]]).
- =wording.mpark.html=: the authored code block names the exposition-only member as =@\exposid{val}@=, the one spelling every backend currently passes through, and that stops mpark/wg21's filter, so =render.sh= writes it as mpark's =$val$= ([[https://github.com/steve-downey/specgen/issues/406][#406]]).

Everything else on the six pages is specgen's output as written.

* The source
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: the-source
:END:

The class body is the synopsis.
The three definitions after it carry the markup, in =//!= comments.
The function bodies, their =static_assert= declarations and the /requires-clause/ are the library's own.

#+transclude: [[file:optional_ref_monadic.hpp]] :src cpp

What each part of the wording is made from:

- =or_else= has one line of markup, =\effects-equiv=.
  Its /Constraints/ is the /requires-clause/, its /Mandates/ is the =static_assert=, and its /Effects/ is the body with the assertion taken out.
- =and_then= takes its /Effects/ from the body the same way.
  Its /Mandates/ is written by hand, because the asserted condition names an implementation detail, and =\covers= says which assertion the sentence stands for.
- =transform= has a hand-written /Mandates/ whose first sentence stands for three assertions, each named by a =\covers=.
  The rest of that paragraph, the note, and /Returns/ have nothing in the code to be checked against.
- The data member is marked =\expos(val)=, so extracted code and backticked prose both print it as the exposition-only name.

A =\covers= that names no assertion is an error, and an assertion that no wording accounts for is reported.

** What the marks are
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: what-the-marks-are
:END:

Each mark has one of two causes.

The implementation differs from the draft:

- =and_then= asserts on =U= where the draft has =remove_cvref_t<U>= ([[https://github.com/steve-downey/optional/issues/119][steve-downey/optional#119]]).
- =transform= has no =remove_cv_t= around =invoke_result_t<F, T&>=, in its declaration and in /Let/ ([[https://github.com/steve-downey/optional/issues/120][steve-downey/optional#120]]).
- =or_else= returns =*this= where the draft returns the contained reference ([[https://github.com/steve-downey/optional/issues/121][steve-downey/optional#121]]).

specgen writes something differently from the draft:

- The local alias =using U = ...;= stays in the /Effects/ code although /Let/ already says it ([[https://github.com/steve-downey/specgen/issues/404][#404]]).
- Extracted code drops =std::= from =std::forward= ([[https://github.com/steve-downey/specgen/issues/405][#405]]).
- The draft's =\tcode{\libconcept{invocable}}= is not read as a concept, so it differs from the generated =\libconcept{invocable}= though the two print alike ([[https://github.com/steve-downey/specgen/issues/407][#407]]).
- The removed closing =>= in the declaration of =transform= is placed after the space that follows it ([[https://github.com/steve-downey/specgen/issues/409][#409]]).

Two more show in the wording itself and not as marks.
The code block inside /Mandates/ for =transform= can name the exposition-only member only with a LaTeX escape, which mpark/wg21 cannot typeset ([[https://github.com/steve-downey/specgen/issues/406][#406]]).
The mpark and org outputs put no space before the parenthesized reference in the note ([[https://github.com/steve-downey/specgen/issues/408][#408]]).

** What typesetting shows
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: what-typesetting-shows
:END:

The [[#rendered-output][typeset pages]] show defects that the files alone do not:

- In =diff.pdf=, a changed code span in prose is written =\removed{\tcode{...}}=, and under wg21-latex it loses the code font and drops characters: the struck /Let/ of =transform= has one closing =>= where the source has two ([[https://github.com/steve-downey/specgen/issues/411][#411]]).
- In both mpark pages, the subclause heading reads "Monadic operations Monadic operations", in the contents too, and the note's reference reads "(General [dcl.init.general])".
  The synopsis comment reads "// Monadic operations [optional.ref.monadic], monadic operations".
  The current mpark/wg21 prints the draft's title beside every stable name written the way specgen writes it ([[https://github.com/steve-downey/specgen/issues/412][#412]]).
- In =diff.org.html=, the removed =*val= in the /Effects/ of =or_else= prints as the literal =\exposid{val}= ([[https://github.com/steve-downey/specgen/issues/413][#413]]).
- In both PDFs, the subclause number prints as a =?= glyph for each part, which is how wg21-latex's =wording= environment shows a number it was not given.
  =specgen generate --section-number= would give it, through wg21-latex's =\clausenumber=, once that macro is merged ([[https://github.com/steve-downey/wg21-latex/pull/2][steve-downey/wg21-latex#2]]).

* Questions for reviewers
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: questions-for-reviewers
:END:

1. A =static_assert(P)= becomes "=P= is =true=", and =static_assert(!P)= becomes "=P= is =false=".
   Several are joined into one sentence with commas and "and".
   Is that the form wanted when the condition is a trait?
2. A body that opens with =using U = ...;= gives /Mandates/ that mention =U=.
   Should the tool write "Let =U= be ..." from the alias and drop the alias from the /Effects/ code?
3. The draft keeps =std::= on =forward= and =move= in code and drops it elsewhere.
   Is that the whole rule?
4. The tool always breaks an item declaration after the template head.
   The draft keeps a short one on one line.
   Does that matter?
5. =requires std::invocable<F>= becomes "=F= models =invocable=".
   Is "models" right for a derived /Constraints/, or should it read "=invocable<F>= is =true="?
6. "The declaration ... is well-formed for some invented variable" has no assertion behind it.
   Is it enough that the tool says which sentences are checked against the code and which are not?
